0.description: Apple scab produces velvety, olive-green to black circular lesions on leaves and fruit, causing premature defoliation and fruit deformity.
0.organic_treatment: Apply liquid copper or sulfur-based sprays before rain events; apply neem oil; rake and burn or compost fallen leaves to eliminate overwintering spores.
0.chemical_treatment: Foliar application of fungicides like Captan, Mancozeb, or Difenoconazole at green tip and pink bud stages.
0.prevention: Plant resistant cultivars (e.g., Liberty, Prima); prune canopy to optimize air circulation and sunlight penetration; avoid overhead watering.

1.description: Produces small purple specks that enlarge into circular lesions with light brown centers ('frogeye' spots) and can cause fruit rot and tree cankers.
1.organic_treatment: Prune out dead wood, fire blight strikes, and cankers during winter; remove mummified fruits from branches and the orchard floor.
1.chemical_treatment: Spray protective fungicides such as Captan, Thiophanate-methyl, or Mancozeb from petal fall through cover sprays.
1.prevention: Ensure good tree vigor; avoid wounding tree bark; maintain balanced nitrogen fertilization; sterilize pruning shears between cuts.

2.description: Characterized by vibrant yellow-orange circular spots on the upper leaf surface that develop tiny black dots and tube-like spore structures beneath.
2.organic_treatment: Apply sulfur or copper soap fungicide at weekly intervals starting at blossom bud emergence; remove nearby wild juniper/cedar host trees within 1-2 miles if possible.
2.chemical_treatment: Apply systemic fungicides containing Myclobutanil or Propiconazole starting from pink bud stage through late spring.
2.prevention: Plant rust-resistant apple cultivars; scout and remove galls from nearby red cedar trees before warm spring rains.

3.description: Leaf tissue exhibits vibrant green chlorophyll, smooth epidermis, and intact vascular venation without necrotic spots or fungal signs.
3.organic_treatment: No curative treatment required. Maintain scheduled balanced organic compost applications.
3.prevention: Continue standard seasonal prophylactic scouting; ensure adequate soil drainage and regular canopy pruning.

4.description: Vibrant, wax-coated green foliage displaying strong cellular structure and balanced micro-nutrient uptake.
4.organic_treatment: Maintain acidic soil pH (4.5 to 5.2) using pine bark mulch and elemental sulfur.
4.prevention: Maintain consistent drip irrigation and acidic rhizosphere conditions.

5.description: Appears as a powdery white-to-gray fungal coating on succulent young foliage and shoot tips, leading to leaf curling and distorted growth.
5.organic_treatment: Spray potassium bicarbonate, horticultural mineral oil, or neem oil; spray diluted fresh milk (1:9 with water) in bright sunlight.
5.chemical_treatment: Apply Triadimefon, Myclobutanil, or wettable sulfur when shoots reach 2-3 inches of growth.
5.prevention: Prune dense canopies to maximize interior airflow and lower humidity; avoid excess early-season nitrogen fertilization.

6.description: Firm green leaf tissue with clear serrated margins and healthy petiole attachment.
6.organic_treatment: No treatment needed. Continue routine organic foliar nutrition.
6.prevention: Maintain orchard sanitation and monitor for early-spring fungal spores.

7.description: Produces rectangular, tan-to-gray necrotic lesions restricted between leaf veins, causing extensive photosynthetic loss and stalk lodging.
7.organic_treatment: Incorporate infected crop residue through clean tillage; rotate with non-host crops like soybean or cotton for at least 1-2 years.
7.chemical_treatment: Apply triazole or strobilurin fungicides (e.g., Azoxystrobin, Pyraclostrobin, or Propiconazole) at VT to R1 growth stages.
7.prevention: Plant corn hybrids with high genetic tolerance to Gray Leaf Spot; optimize plant spacing to avoid dense canopy humidity.

8.description: Small, powdery cinnamon-brown to golden-red pustules on both upper and lower leaf surfaces that rupture the epidermis to release airborne urediniospores.
8.organic_treatment: Plant resistant corn varieties; apply early preventive sprays of bio-fungicides containing Bacillus subtilis.
8.chemical_treatment: Foliar application of strobilurin + triazole combination (e.g., Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole or Pyraclostrobin) when rust pustules first emerge.
8.prevention: Early planting to avoid mid-summer spore flights; monitor lower canopy leaves during cool, damp weather conditions.

9.description: Large, elongated, cigar-shaped grayish-green to tan lesions (1-6 inches long) that develop dark fungal sporulation during moist periods.
9.organic_treatment: Deep tillage to bury infected corn stover; rotate fields with non-grass crops for at least 2 consecutive seasons.
9.chemical_treatment: Apply Mancozeb, Chlorothalonil, or Azoxystrobin when symptoms appear on lower leaves prior to tasseling.
9.prevention: Choose corn hybrids containing Ht-resistance genes; avoid excessive planting density.

10.description: Robust, deep green arching leaf blades displaying clean venation and high photosynthetic vigor.
10.organic_treatment: None needed. Maintain balanced NPK nutrition (nitrogen side-dressing).
10.prevention: Continue standard field scouting and pest monitoring.

11.description: Forms small, circular reddish-brown spots with dark borders on leaves containing black pycnidia pimples; causes infected grapes to shrivel into hard black mummies.
11.organic_treatment: Prune out infected mummies and diseased canes during dormant season; apply copper-based Bordeaux mixture starting at early shoot growth.
11.chemical_treatment: Spray Myclobutanil, Mancozeb, or Captan starting when shoots are 3-5 inches long through post-bloom periods.
11.prevention: Trevising and canopy management to maintain sunny, dry microclimate within grape clusters; clean vineyard floor sanitation.

12.description: Interveinal chlorosis and necrosis creating a distinctive 'tiger-stripe' pattern on leaves; dark spots ('measles') on berries; internal trunk wood decay.
12.organic_treatment: Prune late in the dormant season; paint large pruning wounds immediately with tree wound sealer or Trichoderma bio-protectants.
12.chemical_treatment: No cure for infected wood; apply wound sealants or protective sprays containing Thiophanate-methyl directly to pruning cuts.
12.prevention: Avoid pruning during rainy weather; remove and burn dead vines; inspect vineyard graft unions.

13.description: Produces irregular brown to dark purple necrotic lesions with diffuse yellow halos on older leaves, leading to premature leaf shedding.
13.organic_treatment: Apply copper sulfate or copper hydroxide sprays; collect and destroy fallen leaf debris in autumn.
13.chemical_treatment: Apply protective fungicides such as Mancozeb, Chlorothalonil, or Carbendazim at 14-day intervals.
13.prevention: Improve vineyard air drainage; remove water sprouts and excess foliage around the fruiting zone.

14.description: Broad, vibrant green lobed leaf with crisp margins and clean vascular bundles.
14.organic_treatment: None needed. Maintain balanced micronutrient spray (zinc, boron, iron).
14.prevention: Maintain open canopy structure and regular vineyard sanitation.
